A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Agent-Omit research despite the shortened title. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations on five agent benchmarks, omission experiments, component ablations, and training analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original benchmark results, omission experiments, ablations, and appendix training analyses.

M1.justification: The omission-data synthesis, cold-start training, dual trajectory sampling, rewards, and GRPO objective remain unchanged. Section 4.2 clarifies how partial-trajectory rewards are obtained, consistent with v1's existing description.

E1.justification: Both versions use DeepSearch, WebShop, TextCraft, BabyAI, and SciWorld. Appendix B retains the same constituent DeepSearch datasets, environments, and task requirements.

E2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 retain the same seven frontier models and seven efficiency methods: Thinking-Retention, DEPO, Tool-Light, Observation-Mask, DeepMiner, MEM-Agent, and ReSum. The added related-work citations introduce no evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Model sizes, dataset splits, metrics, interaction budgets, and training configurations in Section 6.1 and Appendix B are unchanged. Figure 3's expanded caption documents the existing experiment without establishing a revised protocol.

E4.justification: The component ablations and reward-weight sensitivity analysis in Figure 5, omission analyses in Figures 2–3 and 6, and training analyses and case study in Appendix C are retained without additional tests.

E5.justification: Neither repeated-run information nor uncertainty-reporting practices change. Figure 3's new statement about averaging over 200 test cases describes sample aggregation, not additional independent runs or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The numerical tables and experimental plots retain their results; the 4B model rows already appeared in v1. For example, both versions report Agent-Omit-8B-RL WebShop Pass@1 of 23.57 and 8,764 average tokens. Appendix C's findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Semantic Lipschitz continuity is reclassified from Lemma 5.1 to Assumption 5.1, with the corresponding change in Appendix A.2, clarifying its status as a premise. The inequalities, omission-error theorem, and derivations remain unchanged, including the appendix's lingering 'Proof' paragraph.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: turn-dependent omission, the two-stage Agent-Omit framework, a KL-based error bound, and effectiveness–efficiency advantages across five benchmarks. The shorter title does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 8 newly acknowledges that additional RL training samples limit scalability. Section 5 adds an explicit monotonic-improvement interpretation of the retained KL bound, while the new impact statement suggests potential energy savings without additional measurements.

D1.justification: Figure 3 now explicitly states that each turn from 1 to 12 is intervened on separately and results are averaged over all 200 randomly sampled test cases. This clarifies the existing analysis; Appendix B's implementation details, hardware, hyperparameters, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds six background references, including AgentBalance, DIMA, UrbanKGent, and MM-Agent. These broaden contextual citations, while the three-way classification of context-management methods and Agent-Omit's distinction from prior work remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, makes localized prose edits, expands the theoretical introduction, and introduces numbered related-work subsections. It also adds conflict-of-interest, acknowledgement, and impact statements and updates author/publication footnotes; the main narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects the mountain-search labels and adds environment icons. Figure 3's caption is expanded, and Tables 2–3 identify the compared model sizes more explicitly. Pagination and spacing shift, but quantitative plots and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly improves clarity and transparency through the corrected Figure 1, more informative Figure 3 caption, explicit assumption labeling, and acknowledgement of RL sampling costs. The empirical evidence and mathematical derivations remain unchanged. The stronger monotonic-improvement wording exceeds what the retained error bound establishes, limiting the theoretical benefit, but the documentation and limitation disclosures provide a small net improvement.
